title: Cascade Prompt-Credit Commitment: Interest on Late Vision Termination Credits (Premium Billing Accounts)
content:
**Commitment.** Under Cascade's prompt-credit commitment, interest is added to the termination credit of a vision plan unit on a Premium Billing Accounts arrangement when the credit is booked late. The interest is added after any deduction and after the floor at 0.00, and the credit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Lateness tiers** (days counted from the unit's termination date to the credit date, in actual calendar days)
| Days from termination date to credit date | Interest added |
|---|---|
| more than 90 | 15 percent a year of the interest base |
| more than 30 and no more than 90 | 10 percent a year of the interest base |
| 30 or fewer | none |

**The interest base.** The unit's filed monthly premium (its Vision Plans plan's monthly premium for its coverage tier) for each month after the termination month that the account had already paid when the credit is booked and that is not among the months already credited — counted as the whole calendar months from the termination date to the account's paid-through date less the months already credited, never fewer than zero, and zero where no paid-through date is on record — running for the days from the unit's termination date to the credit date beyond 30, on an actual-days basis over 365. In words: the filed monthly premium, multiplied by those paid months, multiplied by the days beyond 30, divided by 365; the interest is the tier's yearly percentage of that figure.

*Months already credited* are the months covered by termination credits on the vision line booked since the unit's termination month; a credit counts as booked since that month when the whole calendar months from its booking date to the credit date are no more than the whole calendar months from the termination date to the credit date. Whole months are counted the way an anniversary is counted (a month is complete only when a later month reaches the same day number; the last day of a shorter month does not complete it).

**Boundary points.** 30 days: no interest. 31 days: 10 percent tier. 90 days: 10 percent tier. 91 days: 15 percent tier.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** Filed premium 13.25; termination 31 March; paid-through date 30 June, so 2 whole months (30 June does not complete a third month from 31 March); no months already credited; credit date 30 July, 121 days after termination. Interest base: 13.25 multiplied by 2, multiplied by 91 days beyond 30, divided by 365, about 6.6068. The days exceed 90, so the interest is 15 percent of that, about 0.9910, added unrounded before the final rounding.
